title: Platform Work Directive: Poland will miss the 2 December deadline
lead: The Polish bill implementing Directive (EU) 2024/2831 is still awaiting government approval. The transposition deadline expires on 2 December 2026. What the bill provides and what it means for platforms and fleet partners.
body:
Poland will not transpose the Platform Work Directive on time. EU member states have until 2 December 2026, and the Polish bill (government list no. UC160) has not yet been adopted by the government. After that, it still has to pass the Sejm and the Senate (the lower and upper houses of parliament) and be signed by the President.

## Where the bill stands

The draft Act on Work Performed Through Digital Labour Platforms (*ustawa o wykonywaniu pracy za pośrednictwem cyfrowych platform pracy*) was prepared by the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy. It was added to the government's legislative work programme on 4 August 2026, and its text was published on 6 August. According to the programme, the Council of Ministers is due to adopt it in Q4 2026. The act is to enter into force about one month after publication (status as of 4 November 2026).

Ministry sources told money.pl that the act will not be ready in time. The ministry has not officially given a new date. Poland is not an exception: according to a tracker by Teamed (as of 27 October 2026), no EU member state yet has a fully applicable transposition in force.

## What the bill provides

- **Presumption of employment.** A person working through a platform, including a passenger transport driver, does not have to prove they are an employee. It is the platform that must show there is no employment relationship.
- **Existing contracts.** The presumption will also cover contracts in force on the day the act takes effect, for periods from 2 December 2026.
- **Joint and several liability.** The platform is jointly and severally liable with the intermediary that settles the worker's pay. In passenger transport, this intermediary is usually the fleet partner – a company that handles licences, settlements and often vehicles for app drivers, a typical feature of the Polish market ([see our guide](/en/polish-taxi-market-explained)).
- **Algorithmic management.** Automated decisions, such as blocking an account, are to be subject to human oversight.

> For fleet partners, joint and several liability is the key point. It binds the platform and the intermediary when a worker makes a claim, so the contracts between them may need to change.

## Employers' objections

In the public consultation, employers' organisations argued that the definition of a platform is vague, the presumption arises too easily and the time to rebut it is too short. They also criticised applying the presumption to contracts already concluded. The Polish Association of App Partners (*Polski Związek Partnerów Aplikacyjnych*, PZPA) proposes industry self-regulation. The final shape of the rules will be known after work in the government and parliament.

## What happens after 2 December

Once the deadline passes, the European Commission may open infringement proceedings against a member state (Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union). Whether, and to what extent, the directive's provisions have effect before the Polish act enters into force is disputed. Companies that want to assess their model of cooperation with drivers should consult an employment lawyer.

title: Bolt Drive in Warsaw: the first platform-owned fleet in Poland
lead: At the end of July Bolt launched in-app car rental in Warsaw. It started with almost 400 hybrid Toyotas and announced over PLN 150m (~EUR 34m) of investment in Poland by the end of 2027. What this means for the fleet market.
body:
At the end of July 2026 Bolt launched Bolt Drive in Warsaw – car rental by the minute, hour or day, booked in the app. Almost 400 new hybrid Toyotas appeared in the app at launch. By the end of 2027 the company plans to invest over PLN 150m (~EUR 34m) in developing the fleet and the service in Poland.

## Fleet and rules

- **Cars:** Toyota Yaris and Yaris Cross hybrids with automatic gearboxes. According to Interia, Bolt ordered 300 Yaris cars (Carolina Toyota Wola) and 202 Yaris Cross (Toyota W&J Wiśniewski); more models are to follow.
- **Monitoring:** all cars have third-party liability insurance and a system that scores driving style (Driving Score). The company may contact a driver who drives riskily.
- **Requirements:** at least 23 years of age and a driving licence held for at least one year; document and selfie verification in the app.
- **Pricing:** by time and kilometres, or hourly and daily packages; the system picks the cheaper option. Fees for Warsaw's paid parking zone are included. A 15-minute reservation is free.

Bolt Drive previously operated in Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Germany and the Czech Republic. In Poland it enters a market that Panek left in March 2025 and where Traficar has reduced its presence in many cities.

> Bolt Drive is a service for customers, not cars rented out for passenger transport. It is the first time in Poland that a platform itself buys, services and insures a fleet – in passenger transport these tasks are carried out by fleet partners.

Bolt has not said whether it plans to use its own cars for passenger transport as well (status as of 4 November 2026). For how fleet partners work in Poland, see [our guide to the Polish taxi market](/en/polish-taxi-market-explained).

title: Licence with verification: Poland to tighten rules for foreign taxi drivers
lead: The Ministry of Infrastructure has announced that taxi drivers from outside the EU and EFTA will have to present a criminal-record certificate from their country of origin as well. Today a certificate from the Polish register is enough.
body:
Taxi drivers from outside the European Union and EFTA will have to present a criminal-record certificate from their country of origin, not only from the Polish National Criminal Register (*Krajowy Rejestr Karny*). The change was announced by the Ministry of Infrastructure, RMF24 reported.

Today a person convicted abroad can obtain a licence if they do not appear in the Polish register. The new certificate is to require translation by a sworn translator or certification by a consul.

The industry has been calling for more effective driver verification for months. The topic returns after every high-profile accident involving an app-based driver.

> **Update (4 November 2026):** on 7 July 2026 the ministry added the bill to the government's work programme as UD431. It also covers, among other things, a nationwide driver ID and new duties for intermediaries, such as checking the vehicle's roadworthiness test and taxi liability insurance.

Background: since 17 June 2024 app drivers in Poland must hold a Polish driving licence, and intermediaries must verify each driver in person. See [our guide to the Polish taxi market](/en/polish-taxi-market-explained).
sources: RMF24 — Work not for criminals: changes for taxi drivers (in Polish) — https://www.rmf24.pl/fakty/polska/news-praca-nie-dla-przestepcow-beda-zmiany-dla-kierowcow-taxi,nId,8089932
